links.outcome: In-hospital mortality effect of AI early warning by sociodemographic subgroup (sex, race, ethnicity, language)
links.effect: Overall adjusted HR 0.644 (95% CI 0.532-0.778); consistent across most groups; non-English primary language had greater mortality reduction (adjusted HR 0.419, 95% CI 0.287-0.610, p=0.0082).
links.quote: The CONCERN EWS was significantly associated with reduced risk of in-hospital mortality overall (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.532-0.778, p < 0.0001), with consistent effectiveness across most groups.

links.outcome: Clinician launches of the CONCERN Detailed Prediction Screen by patient demographics
links.effect: Clinicians' Detailed Prediction Screen launches did not significantly differ by sex, race, ethnicity, or primary language, suggesting equitable usage.
links.quote: Clinicians' CONCERN Detailed Prediction Screen launches did not significantly differ by patients' demographic characteristics, suggesting equitable usage.

screen.reason: Evaluates equity in clinician usage and effectiveness of a deployed early warning system across demographic subgroups within a clinical trial, but does not test a specific safeguard/deployment practice intervention.
